name: Arjun main battle tank
overview_md:
The Arjun is India's indigenous main battle tank — a heavy, well-protected vehicle that represents both the achievement and the frustrations of India's drive to design its own armour. Named for the warrior-prince of the Mahabharata and developed over decades by DRDO, it entered Indian Army service from 2004 and equips a small number of armoured regiments in the deserts of the western front against Pakistan.

The Arjun is a capable but heavy tank. It mounts a 120 mm rifled gun (able to fire a gun-launched missile), composite "Kanchan" armour, and a modern fire-control system, and in trials its gunnery and protection have performed well. But at roughly 60–68 tonnes — the Mk1A is among the heaviest tanks in service — it strains India's bridges, rail and logistics, and limits where it can deploy, which has constrained the size of orders.

For an analyst, the Arjun illustrates the tension in Indian defence procurement between indigenous ambition and operational pragmatism. The improved Mk1A added scores of upgrades, and the Army has ordered further batches, but the bulk of India's armour remains the lighter, Russian-derived T-90 Bhishma and T-72. The Arjun is a sovereign capability and a point of national pride, even if it has not displaced imported tanks as the Army's workhorse.

additional.note: Among the heaviest MBTs in service

armament_json.name: 120 mm rifled gun
armament_json.notes: Fires APFSDS, HEAT and gun-launched ATGM (LAHAT)

variants_json.name: Arjun Mk1A
variants_json.key_changes: ~70 upgrades incl. fire control, protection, missile capability

combat_history.event: No combat use; equips Indian Army armoured regiments on the western front.
combat_history.significance: Capability assessed from trials and exercises.

modernization.description: Upgraded Mk1A batches ordered with extensive improvements.
modernization.impact: Sustains an indigenous heavy-armour line alongside imported tanks.

vulnerabilities.description: Very heavy for Indian bridges, rail and logistics.
vulnerabilities.context: Limits where it can deploy; constrains order size.
vulnerabilities.mitigation: Largely confined to the western desert front.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Armoured manoeuvre in the desert terrain of the India–Pakistan western front.
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: Armoured regiments alongside T-90 Bhishma and T-72.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: India's T-90 Bhishma is the lighter, more numerous workhorse; the Arjun is the heavy indigenous tank.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: India's home-grown tank vs its Russian workhorse.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: The Type 99A is China's heavy MBT; both are continental-warfare tanks unlikely to meet given Himalayan terrain.
Pakistan's Chinese-derived tanks the Arjun would face on the western front.

doctrine.role: Indigenous heavy main battle tank for armoured manoeuvre on the western front.
doctrine.employment: Desert armoured operations with a 120 mm rifled gun and heavy composite protection.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Sovereign heavy armour — protection and firepower over strategic mobility.
doctrine.threat_context: A national-pride capability alongside the imported T-90/T-72 mainstay.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against India's T-90 Bhishma, China's Type 99A and Pakistan's VT4/Al-Khalid.
